title: Independent semantic backcheck of silent-slide Study UI candidates
scope: Read-only check of six proposed UI strings across Sesotho (st), Tshivenda (ve), and Xitsonga (ts).
limitations: Meaning/composition check only; no fluent-speaker approval.
No code changes or tests. Candidate strings are not wired.

existingLocaleTermsChecked.stSlides: Diselaete is already used in offlineRegionalSlidesOnly.
existingLocaleTermsChecked.veNarration: courseDeckNoNarration uses ṱhalutshedzo nga ipfi; no verified slide word found in ve locale.
existingLocaleTermsChecked.tsNarration: courseDeckNoNarration uses nhlamuselo hi rito and Xinghezi is present in the current locale; no verified slide word found in ts locale.

rows.literalBackTranslation: “Look at/watch the slides.” The existing Sesotho locale already uses `Diselaete` in `offlineRegionalSlidesOnly`, so the noun is supported in this interface. `Shebella` is a natural action for opening/viewing a slide presentation.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: No meaning risk beyond ordinary review of the command/register.

independentSemanticChecks.languageContamination: Only named English language / expressly provisional English loan `slides`; no accidental full English clause.

rows.sourceEnglish: {count} slides. No narration starts automatically. You can choose English narration.
rows.candidate: Diselaete tse {count}. Ha ho tlhaloso e buuoang e qalang ka boyona. O ka kgetha tlhaloso ya Senyesemane.
rows.literalBackTranslation: “{count} slides. No spoken explanation starts by itself. You can choose an English explanation.” The count is preserved, the negation says nothing starts automatically, and “can choose” keeps English narration optional. `Senyesemane` is the Sesotho name for English.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: No material semantic risk. Candidate matches the existing `courseDeckNoNarration` phrasing for spoken explanation; fluent review still required.

independentSemanticChecks.languageContamination: Only named English language / expressly provisional English loan `slides`; no accidental full English clause.

rows.literalBackTranslation: “Look at the slides.” The polite/plural Tshivenda imperative is clear; `slides` is a provisional English loan, not accidental sentence contamination.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: No established Tshivenda slide term was found in the current locale. Retain `slides` as the requested provisional technical/UI loan pending language review.

independentSemanticChecks.languageContamination: Only named English language / expressly provisional English loan `slides`; no accidental full English clause.

rows.sourceEnglish: {count} slides. No narration starts automatically. You can choose English narration.
rows.candidate: Slides dza {count}. Ṱhalutshedzo nga ipfi a i thomi nga yoṱhe. Ni nga khetha ṱhalutshedzo ya English.
rows.literalBackTranslation: “{count} slides. Spoken explanation does not start by itself. You can choose an English explanation.” The count placeholder, no-auto-start negation, and optional choice all remain.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: `English` is the named language and remains an explicit English loan; the surrounding clause is Tshivenda. No verified local name for English narration was found in the current locale. `slides` is also an intentional provisional loan.

independentSemanticChecks.languageContamination: Only named English language / expressly provisional English loan `slides`; no accidental full English clause.

rows.literalBackTranslation: “See/view the slides.” The imperative is consistent with the singular informal “you” used by this locale; `slides` is an intentional provisional English UI term.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: No established Xitsonga UI word for slides was found in the current locale. Keep the English loan provisional.

independentSemanticChecks.languageContamination: Only named English language / expressly provisional English loan `slides`; no accidental full English clause.

rows.sourceEnglish: {count} slides. No narration starts automatically. You can choose English narration.
rows.candidate: Slides ta {count}. Nhlamuselo hi rito a yi sunguli hi yoxe. U nga hlawula nhlamuselo ya Xinghezi.
rows.literalBackTranslation: “{count} slides. Voice explanation does not start by itself. You can choose an English explanation.” The placeholder is intact; the sentence denies automatic start and makes the English narration selectable rather than required.
rows.meaningRisksAndNotes: `Xinghezi` is already used in the Xitsonga locale (for example, `sidebarBilingualToggle`), so there is no cross-language contamination. `slides` remains a provisional English loan.
